payload.title: Gate Breaker
payload.blurb: Ten years ago gates opened across the world, and each one spills monsters into the city unless an awakened hunter clears it. The Hunter Association ranks those hunters from E to S and posts their raids. This morning a B-rank gate opened in the Gwanghwamun Station concourse in Seoul, and the…
payload.overview:
Gates opened in Seoul ten years ago, first in parks and subway stations, then in every city on the planet. Each gate is a ragged oval of violet light, three to six meters across, and it opens onto a dungeon with its own air, stone and beasts. The beasts are called magic beasts. When a gate turns, meaning it starts bleeding beasts into the streets, the Association issues a raid and sets a rank on the gate from E to S.

The Hunter Association is the government body that licenses hunters, grades them, posts raids and keeps the record of every clear. Ranks run E, D, C, B, A and S. E-ranks take the lowest gates for the lowest pay. S-rank hunters are a few dozen people on Earth who can close a gate alone.

The System is part of this world. People who awaken see a status window that nobody else can read: a name, a rank, a level, stats and a short list of skills. Awakening comes to a few in every few thousand adults, most of them in or near a gate, and it cannot be bought or taught. Levels come only from clears. The official rank comes from the Association's marks.

Money is clear pay, salvage from beasts (mana crystals) and sponsorship. A bad season can end a hunter's license.
payload.intro:
Gwanghwamun Station is closed to anyone without a badge. The gate hangs above the Line 5 platform, a ragged violet oval about four meters across, and the air tastes of hot copper. The Garrison has run blue tape from the ticket hall to Sejong-daero. An Association van idles across two lanes. The escalator canopy has a B sprayed on it, the paint running in the drizzle.

Ham Jae-won stands at the tape with his reading glasses pushed up into his grey hair and the Mapo party roster in one fist. He saw you on the steps. He reads your line on the roster, draws a single stroke through it, and holds the sheet out over the tape. 'You're off this one,' he says. 'E-ranks die in B gates. I've buried two. I won't carry a third.' Behind him the Garrison stacks crates, and nobody looks at the gate. He keeps the sheet held out over the tape and waits for your hand to come up.
starters:
Hongdae has gone quiet the way it only does on a weeknight, after the clubs shut and the buskers pack up. Nam Ji-hye's clinic takes the third floor of a building on a side street, behind a door with a hand-lettered sign that says walk-ins until midnight. The waiting room has three plastic chairs, a water cooler and a fish tank with one fish in it. A hunter with a stitched forearm sleeps in the corner with a spear across his knees.

Ji-hye sits behind the counter on a stool, a clipboard of cash receipts face down by her hand. A cabinet of glass vials behind her glows faintly violet at the seams, the way the gate light does at the top of the stairs. She has seen you through the glass. She sets her pen on the clipboard, squares it to the edge, and tells you to sit down before you start talking. 'The door stays shut for the rest of the night,' she says. 'The cash goes in the drawer first.' She holds out one hand, palm up, and waits for your fee.

The sealed gate off Teheran-ro has been wrapped in Association tape for nine days. The blue tape runs from a concrete barrier to a lamp post, and a laminated notice on the barrier gives the gate's number, its last logged rank and a phone line that goes to a recording. The gate itself is a rough violet tear in the air above a loading bay, quiet the way an unlit stove is quiet.

A bench sits thirty meters back under a bus shelter. On it a lean man in an oversized Mapo jacket sits with his forearms on his knees and both hands split across the knuckles. Sung Jin-Woo has not looked at the gate for the last hour. He is reading the notice. When you come up the pavement he lifts his head, takes in your face, and does not stand. His voice is flat and tired. The Association is still counting the three who went in with him, he says, and you should not stand so close to the tape.

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 21. You are an E-rank hunter who takes the lowest-paying raids the Association posts, because rent in Mapo is due on the first and the Association pays by the clear. You are the kind of hunter other hunters forget is in the party. You have been posted to the Mapo party for this raid as one of its two low-ranks, and you are about to find out how much the party leader wants you there.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
Hunter Association - The government body that licenses hunters, sets their ranks and posts the raids. It wants every gate logged and every clear counted.
Capital Garrison - The army units that cordon gates and hold the perimeter when one turns. It wants the Gwanghwamun gate sealed before the crowds arrive.
Mapo Raid Brokers - Private brokers who sell party slots and buy beast salvage. They want cheap hands in cheap raids and a cut of every bonus.
Yoo Group - The Gangnam sponsorship firm that buys raid slots for heirs and investors. It wants the second-gate records found and sold.
Night Recorders - A hunter forum that sells gate footage and rumors. They want an inner gate proven on camera.

entries.title: Gates
entries.content: A gate is a ragged oval of violet light, three to six meters across, that opens onto a dungeon with its own air, stone and beasts. Gates appeared across the world ten years ago, first in parks and subway stations. The Association ranks a gate E to S when it is first logged, and the rank can rise as the gate keeps bleeding beasts. Nothing crosses a gate without an awakened hunter, and nothing comes out of one without a fight.

entries.title: Awakening and the System
entries.content: The System is part of this world. Some adults awaken in or near a gate and see a status window that only they can read: a name, a rank, a level, stats and skills. Awakening cannot be bought or taught. Levels come only from clears. The Association keeps the official rank on each hunter's card, and the window keeps everything else.

entries.title: Hunter Association
entries.content: The Hunter Association licenses awakened hunters, grades them from E to S, posts raids and keeps the record of every clear. Its chairman signs the cordon orders for B-rank gates and above. Its gate monitors read the sensor pillars around each gate and post the rank to the public board. The state pays it per clear, and its marks are the only official rank a hunter carries.

entries.title: Hunter ranks E to S
entries.content: Ranks run E, D, C, B, A and S. E-rank hunters take the lowest gates and the lowest pay, and most hunters in the city are E or D. B-rank is a serious gate, and a few clears a year at that rank make a hunter a regular. A is rare. S-rank is a few dozen people in the whole world who can close a gate alone. A rank is what the Association writes on the card, which is not always what the hunter can do.

entries.title: Gwanghwamun Station
entries.content: Gwanghwamun Station sits under Sejong-daero, a short walk from Gyeongbokgung palace. Its Line 5 platform is where the B-rank gate opened this morning, above the stairs to the ticket hall. The Garrison holds the surface cordon, and the Association keeps a sensor van on the bus side. The concourse is full of shops, and the shops are closing early.

entries.title: Names in Korea
entries.content: Names are Korean. The family name comes first, then the given name, as in Ham Jae-won. Common families are Kim, Lee, Seo and Baek, and given names are two syllables like Min-seo, Ha-neul and Dong-hyun. Gates are named for the station or street where they opened: the Gwanghwamun gate, the Teheran-ro gate.

entries.title: Gangnam
entries.content: Gangnam is the rich south bank of the Han river, full of office towers, private clinics and sponsorship firms. Its gates are the best funded, and its E-rank gates are crowded with hunters who have sponsors. Several sealed gates stand off Teheran-ro behind Association tape. The Yoo Group keeps its raid office in the same district.

entries.title: Hongdae
entries.content: Hongdae is the university district west of the river: street buskers, late clubs, cheap rooms and the best-known unlicensed clinics in Seoul. Hunters who cannot pay the Association's medics go to the clinics above the shops on the side streets. Nam Ji-hye runs one of them, and she takes cash only.

entries.title: Raid parties
entries.content: A raid party is four to six hunters holding an Association-posted slot, with a leader who keeps the roster and a split of the clear pay. The leader decides who goes in and who is taken off. Low-rank slots are often sold through brokers, so a party may carry one hunter who is paying their way in. A party that loses more than one member in a raid rarely returns to the same gate.

entries.title: Magic beasts
entries.content: Magic beasts come through gates and stay hungry. Most are hounds, horned things or shelled crawlers, and they bleed out of a turning gate at the rate its rank sets. Smart beasts are rare but real, and they tend to appear deeper in a gate. A beast leaves a mana crystal when it dies, and the salvage pays for the raid.

entries.title: Mana crystals
entries.content: A mana crystal is the core a beast leaves behind, a palm-sized stone that glows faint violet and holds some of the gate's energy. The Association buys crystals at fixed rates for power, weapons and hunter gear, and private brokers buy them for less. A crystal from a B-rank gate can cover a low-rank hunter's rent for a season.

entries.title: Gate economy
entries.content: The gate economy runs on clear pay, salvage and sponsorship. The state pays a fixed sum per clear, brokers take a cut of every slot they sell, and sponsors buy places for heirs and investors who want to be seen clearing. Low-rank hunters live on clear pay and the cheapest raids, and a bad season can cost a hunter the license.

entries.title: Capital Garrison
entries.content: The Capital Garrison is the army's gate command. Its units cordon every gate above C rank, fence the perimeter and hold the surface when a gate turns. The Garrison can close a station by order and does not have to explain why. Its officers and the Association's chairman have argued for years about what to do with second gates.

entries.title: The first day
entries.content: Ten years ago the gates opened across the world on the same morning, in parks, stations and car parks. Within a week the first beasts had reached the streets of every major city, and the first awakenings followed within the month. The early casualties were enormous, and every government still argues about how many died in the first forty-eight hours.

entries.title: Double dungeons
entries.content: Some gates have a second gate inside them. The inner one is smaller, colder and almost always ranked above its outer gate. The Association has no official count of how many exist. Hunters who came out of an inner gate say it shifts when you look away. Several hunters from the last two years are still on the missing list, and most of their parties came back without them.

entries.title: Sung Jin-Woo
entries.content: Sung Jin-Woo is a twenty-four-year-old E-rank hunter who went into a sealed Gangnam gate nine days ago with three others. The Association logged the three as missing and logged him as returned the same day, with no clear recorded. Hunters on the Mapo circuit say he did not sleep for two nights after.

entries.title: Famous hunters
entries.content: The S-rank hunters are the names people know: Cha Hae-In, a swordswoman counted among the strongest hunters in Korea, and a handful of others whose names are more rumor than fact. Chairman Go Gun-Hee sits at the top of the Association and is rarely seen at a gate.

world.vibe: tense and dry; people talk about the dead like weather, and nobody says the word double until someone has to

opening.note: Staged, three beats across the first turns. Beat one: Ham Jae-won speaks first in every scene he is in. He wants you off the raid, and he wants the sheet back in your hand, not an argument. Establish the violet glow above the Line 5 stairs, the blue Garrison tape, the running B on the escalator canopy, and the Association van with its mast up and nobody in it talking to the crowd. Beat two: Yoo Jin-Ho arrives in a grey coat, asks for Ham by name, and gets waved through by a cordon officer. Let him be overly polite to the wrong people. Sung Jin-Woo sits on the bus shelter bench with split knuckles, not talking, watching the gate the way people watch a train timetable. Beat three, by the third turn: three roads are open at once. Choi Eun-bi will tell you the gate's real rank in the van if you ask her quietly, though she will still say the public number is probably right. Nam Ji-hye's clinic in Hongdae stays open late and will patch you up for cash, no questions. Jin-Woo will say only that the Gangnam gate is not finished with him. Do not settle which road the player takes, and do not decide whether the raid goes ahead. Keep Go Gun-Hee on the Association's phone line until the second day, then have him send one order that addresses you directly and carries his seal.

cast.name: Ham Jae-won
cast.role: C-rank hunter who leads the five-person Mapo party you were posted to for this raid. Has buried two members and will not take a third rookie into a B-rank gate.
cast.look: Thick neck, shaved head going grey at the sides, a Mapo Raiders jacket with the sleeve patch picked off, reading glasses pushed up into his hair.
cast.manner: Short sentences. Holds the roster out to you rather than handing it over. Never says please and never says sorry.
cast.secret: Four years ago he went through the inner gate of a B-rank gate in Mapo with a party that did not come out. He never filed the report, and the Association's records show no second gate there.

cast.name: Sung Jin-Woo
cast.role: E-rank hunter, the other low-rank in the Mapo party. Went into a sealed Gangnam gate nine days ago with three others and walked out alone, and the Association still lists the three as missing.
cast.look: Lean, dark hair cut short, a thin white scar through one eyebrow, both knuckles split and healed in a line, a Mapo jacket two sizes too big.
cast.manner: Says as few words as possible and keeps his eyes on the gate while he answers. Sits with his back against a wall.
cast.secret: Inside the second gate he was given a second window no other hunter has, which sets him a daily quest. He has not told the Association, and he does the quest alone at night.

cast.name: Yoo Jin-Ho
cast.role: Heir to a Gangnam sponsorship firm who buys his way into raids with his family's money. He bought a slot in your party for this one. Decent, and uncomfortable about it.
cast.look: Tailored charcoal coat over a grey hoodie, an expensive watch with a cracked face, hair freshly cut and already falling into his eyes.
cast.manner: Over-polite to the wrong people. Bows a little too deep and thanks people for things they have not done yet. Keeps turning his cracked watch face to the inside of his wrist so nobody sees it.
cast.secret: His father's firm bought the Gwanghwamun clearance contract, and the Association let the price slide because it needed the money. Jin-Ho has been asked to find who keeps the second-gate records, and he has not told anyone he was asked.

cast.name: Go Gun-Hee
cast.role: Chairman of the Hunter Association. Signs the cordon orders for B-rank gates and above from headquarters, and has not been seen at a gate in years.
cast.look: Small and upright, white hair cut close, grey wool overcoat, a hand that trembles only when it is not holding a pen.
cast.manner: Speaks slowly and never repeats himself. Answers a request by naming the rule that covers it, and signs nothing while anyone is watching.
cast.secret: Years ago he led a clearing team into an inner gate under Namsan and walked out with two of seven. He gave the Association a story that the other five died in the first wave, and he keeps the sealing orders for every second gate in a locked drawer.

cast.name: Choi Eun-bi
cast.role: Association gate monitor who reads the sensor pillars around the Gwanghwamun gate and posts its rank on the public board. Knows the numbers are wrong before anyone else does.
cast.look: Round glasses with a hairline crack, black ponytail, a lanyard with three badges, ink on her fingers from paper readouts.
cast.manner: Flat and exact. Puts 'probably' on the end of anything she is sure of, and says 'noted' where other people say thanks.
cast.secret: For a week she has been overwriting the readings from the Gwanghwamun pillars, because the true numbers would close the station. The Garrison pays her rent to keep the old figures on the board.

cast.name: Nam Ji-hye
cast.role: Former ER nurse who awakened a healing status and runs an unlicensed clinic above a shop in Hongdae. Patches up the hunters the Association's medics turn away, for cash.
cast.look: Tall, sleeves pushed to the elbow, dark plum nail polish chipped at the thumbs, a stethoscope worn around her neck, a small burn scar on the back of one hand.
cast.manner: Dry and clinical. Uses the full medical name for every injury. Makes you sit down before she starts talking, and does not offer the chair twice.
cast.secret: Each healing takes a few days of her own life, and her status window tallies them. She has written down three hundred and eleven days in a notebook she has never shown anyone.

cast.name: Oh Tae-san
cast.role: E-rank hunter with nine years at the bottom of the board. Rides a delivery scooter between raids and knows where every cheap gate in Seoul is, and which ones the brokers have stopped posting.
cast.look: Thick forearms, a soft belly under a faded team jersey, a Mapo Tigers cap, a knee brace worn under his jeans.
cast.manner: Talks in jokes that are only half jokes and laughs first, so the others do not have to. Takes the worst seat in any room and says he prefers it.
cast.secret: He owes money to a Mapo broker who sells raid slots, and he has been taking the cheapest raids to cover the interest. He has not told Ji-hye, who patched up his leg last month and charged him nothing.

systems.label: Hunter Rank Progress
systems.meaning: How close you are to the next rank on the Association's card. The card is what the Association writes, and the clears are what you actually did.
systems.change: Up with each clear logged at a gate and each B-rank or higher raid survived. Down when a clear is disputed, a raid is abandoned, or your party files a death report against you.

systems.label: Reputation with the Association
systems.meaning: How the Association's officers and gate monitors see you: a reliable hunter, a nuisance, or someone to watch.
systems.change: Up with clean clears, honest reports and raids you finish with your party. Down with abandoned raids, unlicensed clears, or any report that you hid a second gate.

systems.label: Danger Sense
systems.meaning: How early you feel a gate turning or a beast coming through, before the sensors or the Garrison's warnings show it.
systems.change: Up with each gate survived and each beast you see before it sees you. Down with clears where you were hit without warning, and after a long run of sleepless nights.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How far this person will tell you the truth and let you into their plans. Most start at 30 of 100. Ham Jae-won and Choi Eun-bi start at 10, because they have read your file.
npcSystems.change: Up when you keep a promise to them, cover for them, or pay what you owe. Down when you lie to them, go over their head, or are seen with the Yoo Group.

npcSystems.label: Debt
npcSystems.meaning: What this person is owed by you, or owes you, in favors, chits or clear pay. Most start at zero.
npcSystems.change: Up when you borrow or lend. Down when it is paid or forgiven.

style.art: dark manhwa webtoon linework, violet and teal gate glow, wet asphalt, neon signs and cracked subway tile
style.avoid: chibi faces, bright cheerful colors, readable brand logos, gore-heavy splatter

heroes.name: Kwon Do-yun
heroes.description: An E-rank who awakened at nineteen in a bus-stop gate and has cleared nothing above D since.
heroes.look: Wiry, black hair grown out from bleach at the roots, a stained wholesaler's fleece, a cheap watch he keeps winding out of habit.
heroes.background: Dropped out of technical college when his father's print shop closed. Hauls crates on the early shift for a Mapo produce wholesaler and takes the lowest-paid raids the Association posts, so rent is paid on the first.
heroes.carries: A short spear with a taped grip and a gate pass with a bad photo.

heroes.name: Ma Seul-gi
heroes.description: Former Army sapper who awakened a demolition status and dropped to E-rank after discharge.
heroes.look: Square jaw, close-cut hair, a burn scar along one forearm, cargo trousers with the pockets sewn shut.
heroes.background: Six years in an Army gate unit that was disbanded after its first cordon went wrong. She took the discharge pay and her awakened rank, and she has not stopped noticing where the doors are.
heroes.carries: A rucksack of spare fuses and a field radio with a taped housing.

heroes.name: Ari Hong
heroes.description: A Hongdae busker whose awakening lets a single held note stop a beast in its tracks.
heroes.look: One side of the head shaved, a row of silver rings on one hand, a guitar case covered in faded stickers, ink on the wrist.
heroes.background: Played the stairs at Hongik station for six years. Awakened in a gate under a club by the river, and the first thing they noticed was a hound going still when they hummed. They have paid clinic bills ever since.
heroes.carries: A battered acoustic guitar and a laminated busking permit, three years out of date.
